references.text: Psalm 118:22 speaks of the stone that the builders rejected, which became the cornerstone. This points prophetically to the rejection of the Son of Man by the elders, chief priests, and scribes, as Jesus predicts in Luke 9:22.

Isaiah 53:3 describes the Lord's suffering servant as despised and forsaken by men, a man of sorrows, well acquainted with sickness. This is a prophetic parallel to Jesus' prediction that the Son of Man must suffer greatly.

Isaiah 53:10 states that it was the Lord's will to crush his servant with suffering. The word 'Δεῖ' (it is necessary) in Luke 9:22 emphasizes the divine necessity of the suffering, as foretold in Isaiah.
Hosea 6:2 says "on the third day he will raise us up", which points to Jesus' resurrection on the third day, a central part of the prediction in Luke 9:22.

Matthew 16:21 is a direct parallel where Jesus begins to explain to his disciples that he must go to Jerusalem and suffer greatly from the elders, chief priests, and scribes, be killed, and rise on the third day.
Matthew 17:22-23 is another prediction of suffering where Jesus tells them that the Son of Man will be handed over into human hands, be killed, and rise on the third day.

Mark 8:31 is the closest parallel in the Gospel of Mark, where Jesus teaches that the Son of Man must suffer greatly, be rejected by the elders, chief priests, and scribes, be killed, and rise after three days.
Mark 9:31 is the second prediction of suffering in Mark, where Jesus again predicts his death and resurrection.
Luke 17:25 repeats the theme that the Son of Man must first suffer greatly and be rejected by this generation, reinforcing the message in Luke 9:22.
Luke 18:31-33 is the third prediction of suffering in the Gospel of Luke, where Jesus describes in detail his suffering, death, and resurrection on the third day.
Luke 24:7 refers back to Jesus' own prediction that the Son of Man must be handed over into the hands of sinful men, be crucified, and rise on the third day – a direct fulfillment of Luke 9:22.
Luke 24:46 summarizes after the resurrection that Christ had to suffer and rise from the dead on the third day, as it was written – confirming the prediction in 9:22.
Acts 4:10-11 proclaims that Jesus of Nazareth was crucified and raised by God, and that he is the stone rejected by the builders. This connects rejection, death, and resurrection from Luke 9:22.
1 Corinthians 15:4 confirms that Christ was buried and rose on the third day according to the Scriptures, which is the apostolic confirmation of what Jesus predicted in Luke 9:22.
